ignoreValues.reason: The warm Paper ground (#f4efe4) is a made decision, not a reflex reach for the safe off-white. It was chosen over a near-white specifically because pure-white cards on near-white read as glare; see DESIGN.md, Paper not near-white. The rule is right that cream is an AI default; it is wrong that this one is.

The Arcade is a cabinet. Colored glow on the ribbons, LEDs and slot chips IS the subject of the page, not a cool-looking default applied to a generic UI. Scoped to /games only — a glow anywhere else on the site is still a finding.

The ARCADE wordmark is the one display moment on the site and the gradient is the marquee. Decorative by intent and not load-bearing for meaning. Scoped to /games; gradient text on a heading anywhere else is still a finding.
CRT scanlines. The point of the page is that it looks like a cabinet from 1985.
Cabinet edge lighting on the game cards — the thin border plus wide colored shadow reads as a lit machine, which is the intent. Same scoping logic as dark-glow.

Market Storm reports render financial data tables (the earnings print, valuation multiples) whose rows exceed the ~80-char prose measure by necessity — a scannable data row is not a prose reading line, which is what this rule protects. ALL actual prose in these reports is explicitly capped at 62ch (summary, analysis, bull/bear items, verification, callouts, the hero verdict). Scoped to /market-storm so an over-wide prose paragraph anywhere else on the site is still caught.
